subject: DPA redlines: snapshot handover, backup copies, and erase acknowledgement timeline
messages:
From: EmberPay Legal <legal@emberpay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Raman <asha.raman@emberpay.com>; EmberPay Ops <ops@emberpay.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EmberPay DPA redline questions: snapshots/backups & erase timing

Logan —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. We reviewed the retention/delete sections and had a few operational questions we couldn't reconcile with our internal compliance controls. Attached is our redline (EmberPay_DPA_Redline_20290327.pdf). High level:

- Definition scope: your DPA references "snapshots" and "backups" but doesn't make operational distinctions. Are backups included in the same "erase window" as primary data?
- Erase acknowledgement: EmberPay needs a written acknowledgement that deletion operations include any customer-specific snapshots or cold backups within the same jurisdiction. Can Redwood provide an SLA for the erase acknowledgement timeline?
- Escrow/restore: in the event of restoration requests, what is the maximum time you retain customer-held snapshots that could be restored?

We understand some low-level infrastructure constraints exist (replication delays, cross-zone copies). If you can provide proposed language to the DPA that maps to your operational playbook (including realistic timelines), that will help our legal & compliance teams.

Requesting a quick call tomorrow to walk through the proposed language.

Thanks,
Dana Keller
Senior Counsel, EmberPay
legal@emberpay.com

Attachments: EmberPay_DPA_Redline_20290327.pdf (Redline PDF)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: EmberPay Legal <legal@emberpay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay DPA redline questions: snapshots/backups & erase timing

Dana —

Appreciate the redline and questions. Quick responses up front:

- Backups vs snapshots: we operate with two classes — (1) operational snapshots (point-in-time images tied to a tenant for restore/testing) and (2) system backups (multi-tenant, storage-layer backups used for disaster recovery). Our default DPA treats tenant-bound operational snapshots as "customer copies" subject to erase requests; system backups are retained for DR but we can scope access controls and onshore/offshore placement.
- Erase acknowledgement: we can commit to an "erase acknowledgement" within 5 business days confirming action started and listing impacted storage locations; final completion confirmation will be provided once background validation and tombstoning has completed (timeline below).
- Restore retention: we keep tenant operational snapshots for up to 60 days by default, but that can be reduced to 30 days for customers who require shorter windows.

I'll loop Jordan (legal ops) and Marissa (product/security) into operational constraints so we can propose clean DPA language. Suggested next step: 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through our proposed paragraph and a diagram I'll attach.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-erase-clause-20290328.docx (proposed clause)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: EmberPay Legal <legal@emberpay.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 12:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed operational language + timeline

Dana / Asha —

Following up from Logan's note with the operational fallback language we suggest adding into Section 4.2 (Erase & Copies). I'm pasting the suggested paragraph here for ease of review; the attached DOCX contains the same in tracked-changes.

Proposed clause (operationally-aligned):
"

For the purposes of this Agreement: (a) "Operational Snapshot" means a tenant-bound point-in-time copy of Customer Data used for restore, rollback, or tenant-level testing; (b) "System Backup" means storage-layer copies maintained for disaster recovery that may contain deduplicated or aggregated data across customers.

Redwood will treat Operational Snapshots as Customer Data and will, upon receipt of a valid deletion request, (i) initiate an erase operation within five (5) business days and provide an Erase Initiation Acknowledgement to Customer; (ii) propagate deletions to all known tenant-bound copies and mark tombstones within thirty (30) calendar days; (iii) surface a Completion Confirmation once tombstoning and verification checks finish, anticipated within forty-five (45) calendar days of initiation, subject to the exceptions in Section 4.2. System Backups are excluded from the 30-day tombstone requirement but Redwood will: (A) maintain access controls to prevent restore of customer-specific data from System Backups after an erase completion confirmation; and (B) retain System Backups only for disaster recovery and delete them in accordance with our retention schedule, except where retention is required by law.
"

Operational notes (clarifications):
- Asynchronous replication to cold archives can introduce a lag of up to 7 days; we will include discovery of such copies in the Erase Initiation Acknowledgement.
- Onshore carve-outs: if you require strict onshore-only retention, we can offer a per-account operational runbook and increased deletion visibility (audit logs) as an Addendum.

If that language looks close to what you need, Logan and I can accept a small edits call and then push a counter-redline.

Jordan Blake
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@emberpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed operational language + timeline

Jordan —

Thanks, that paragraph helps. A few follow-ups from compliance/ops review:

1) "Completion Confirmation" timing — our policy requires evidence of deletion for any tenant-bound snapshot within 30 days, ideally with a hash/time-stamped log entry for attestation. Your 45-day completion timeline is a gap for us.
2) System Backup carve-out — we need clarity that System Backups will be logically segregated by jurisdiction or, if not possible, that restores are blocked and an attestation provided that no customer-specific restoration occurred after erase.
3) For the Erase Initiation Acknowledgement, EmberPay expects a short inventory of locations (region, storage-class) where copies were found and an estimate for when each will be tombstoned.

Can Redwood do a middle ground: 30-day completion confirmation for Operational Snapshots, with an optional 15-day extension only by mutual agreement and only if we receive logs showing progress? Also please confirm whether the 7-day replication lag refers to cold-archival ingestion only or applies to all cross-zone snapshots.

We can do a call at 10:00 PT to iron this out.

Best,
Asha Raman
Lead, Vendor Compliance
EmberPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@emberpay.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed operational language + timeline

Asha —

Thanks for the specifics. Operationally, we can meet EmberPay halfway with the following commitments:

- Revised completion commitment: Completion Confirmation for Operational Snapshots within thirty (30) calendar days of Erase Initiation, provided Customer does not have an active hold request; Redwood may extend by up to fifteen (15) calendar days solely with documented technical reasons, in which case Redwood will provide incremental status logs every 72 hours.
- Attestation artifacts: Redwood will provide a deletion evidence bundle that includes time-stamped tombstone events and storage-location inventory (region + storage class). Where cryptographic hashes are not available due to storage-layer deduplication, we will provide correlating metadata and timestamps sufficient for attestation.
- System Backup handling: System Backups will be prevented from being used to restore customer-specific data after a Completion Confirmation; we will provide a restore-block attestation and a statement of any multi-tenant storage retention that remains for DR. If EmberPay opts for onshore-only backups, we will provide a runbook and additional logging as an addendum.

I attached a simple diagram that maps our replication/backup tiers to the timelines above (snapshot-handover-sequence.png). If that aligns with EmberPay's compliance needs, Jordan and Logan will convert to tracked DPA language and circulate a clean counter.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
